'''Brigitte Pakendorf''' (born 1970)<ref name="birth">{{cite web|url=https://archive.mpi.nl/tla/islandora/object/tla%3A1839_00_0000_0000_001A_7B4F_7|title=Solodikov_AA_Tabun_1|website=The Language Archive|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref> is a [[linguistics|linguist]] and [[population genetics|geneticist]] at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS).<ref name="ae">{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pakendorf_Brigitte|title=Brigitte Pakendorf|website=Academia Europaea|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref>

==Education==
After receiving her MA in [[biological anthropology]] in 1996, Pakendorf studied for two doctorates: one in biology, one in linguistics. She received the former in 2001 from the [[University of Hamburg]] and the latter in 2007 from the [[University of Leiden]].<ref name="ae-cv">{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Pakendorf_Brigitte/CV|title=Brigitte Pakendorf - Curriculum Vitae|website=Academia Europaea|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref> This second thesis brought together her interests in dealing with contact in the prehistory of the Sakha, or [[Yakuts]], from both linguistic and genetic perspectives. It received the 2008 prize for the best dissertation in linguistics defended at a Dutch university, awarded jointly by the Dutch Association for General Linguistics (AVT) and Association for Applied Linguistics (Anéla).<ref name="ae-cv"/><ref name="avt">{{cite web|url=https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/avt/dissertatieprijs|title=AVT/Anéla Dissertatieprijs|language=nl|website=University of Leiden|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref>

==Career and honours==
From 2006 to 2012 Pakendorf was leader of a [[Max Planck Society]] junior research group on Comparative Population Linguistics at the [[Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology]] in [[Leipzig]]. In 2012 she took up a position as senior researcher (DR2) at the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS) in the laboratory ''Dynamique du langage'' (Language dynamics). She was promoted to senior researcher first class (DR1) in 2016, and exceptional class (DRCE) in 2018.<ref name="ae"/>

Pakendorf has received numerous honours and awards for her research. In 2016 she was awarded a [[CNRS Silver Medal]].<ref name="cnrs">{{cite web|url=https://www.cnrs.fr/fr/talents/cnrs?medal=39&year=2016|title=Médaille d'argent du CNRS|website=CNRS|date=September 2016 |language=fr|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref> In 2019 she was elected member of the [[Academia Europaea]].

==Research==
Pakendorf's research is interdisciplinary, bridging [[biology]], [[anthropology]] and linguistics. She works on languages of Siberia, in particular [[Even language|Even]], [[Negidal language|Negidal]] and other [[Tungusic languages]].<ref name="ae"/><ref name="ae-cv"/> The topics that she has investigated include [[prehistory]], [[language contact]], [[linguistic typology]], [[geolinguistics|areal linguistics]], [[molecular anthropology]], and [[language documentation]].<ref name="ae"/> She has received major grants from the [[German Research Foundation]], Endangered Languages Documentation Programme, [[Louis Leakey#Prominent organizations|Leakey Foundation]], [[Volkswagen Foundation]] and [[Axel Wenner-Gren#Personal life|Wenner-Gren Foundation]] to investigate and document the languages and history of the groups mentioned above.<ref name="ae-cv"/><ref name="dfg">{{cite web|url=https://gepris.dfg.de/gepris/person/27030095?language=en|title=Professorin Dr. Brigitte Pakendorf|website=DFG: GEPRIS|language=de|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref><ref name="volks">{{cite web|url=https://portal.volkswagenstiftung.de/search/personDetails.do?addrNum=24319&fromProject=89394|title=Person: Dr. Dr. Brigitte Pakendorf|website=Volkswagen Stiftung|language=de|access-date=3 March 2024}}</ref>
